title: Gwinnett couple warn others after losing $800K in cryptocurrency scam

reading.body:
A retired Georgia couple lost nearly $800,000 to a cryptocurrency investment scam that deployed an AI-generated fake website. The scam began with an unsolicited WhatsApp message and proceeded through classic social engineering: the fraudster allowed small successful trades and withdrawals to build trust before soliciting a large investment that never existed.

The failure occurred at the point where the couple relied on a mobile trading app without independent verification of its legitimacy. The scammers created a deceptive overlay on a real app that displayed false account balances and fabricated investment gains. This is a case of impersonation and fraud enabled by AI-generated assets, not a failure of the AI system itself to perform as designed.

It is not established whether the couple had any way to distinguish the fraudulent overlay from a legitimate interface, or what security features the actual app possessed.

reports.title: Georgia couple loses $800K in sophisticated cryptocurrency scam
Gwinnett couple warn others after losing $800K in cryptocurrency scam

summary:
A retired Georgia couple lost nearly $800,000 in a sophisticated cryptocurrency scam that started with a WhatsApp message from a stranger. The scammer convinced Jerry Dunaway to invest in cryptocurrency through a mobile trading app, gradually building trust by allowing him to make small trades and withdraw modest amounts. However, the entire scheme was fraudulent, using an AI-generated fake website that displayed false investment balances and made it appear that money was growing.

When Jerry attempted to make a larger withdrawal, he discovered the funds were gone and contacted police. Gwinnett County investigators confirmed the app itself was real but scammers had created a deceptive overlay to manipulate what Jerry saw on screen. Though the couple is cooperating with law enforcement, police say victims in these cases rarely recover their money. Their children have started a GoFundMe campaign to help the Dunaways with daily expenses, and the couple is publicly warning others about the sophisticated tactics used by these criminals.
